packet-14 -- isolated first reading (unverified image reading)
No identification of the work or author was revealed in my context. I did nothing beyond the reader rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (written from overviews as each is viewed)

image-001 (overview, face 1): two separate pieces shot together.
 - Left: small irregular fragment (shelfmark slip reads "Stams, StA, Frag. 82-1r"?). Large decorative calligraphic display script: "[..]seph" with a flourished capital after it, below "Organista", below "Anno" with flourish. A grey rectangle (redaction/placeholder patch) is pasted over the lower part in the image. Looks like a title/label leaf (a name + "Organista" + "Anno ..."), not running text.
 - Right: a paper leaf, single column, ~22 lines of a fast 16th-century-style cursive (humanist/chancery italic, Latin). Heading line at top centre: "M D xxx[..] Die Martis [..] Martii"(?). Text begins with enlarged "Cum". A paragraph break ~line 8 begins "De ...". Vertical crease/stain down middle. Slip lower right "Stams, StA, Frag. 82-2r"(?). No columns, no glosses, no rubrics visible.

TRANSCRIPTION

image-002 (native tile, upper-left of face 1; mostly black background). Shows only the left margin and first word(s) of each line of the right-hand paper leaf, plus the top of the small fragment.
Right leaf, line starts (line numbers counted from top of this image):
 002.1  Cum Cor[..] with superscript "mis" (abbrev., Cor(?)mis ...) ; large looped C
 002.2  Regiis(?) ut [..]   (written "Regijs"? with flourish below)
 002.3  vlterius m[..]
 002.4  Illud in qua[..]
 002.5  Remm(?)/Regni(?) ips[..]
 002.6  vt viudus(?) [..]
 002.7  Reg(?) [..] ro[..]   (abbreviated, flourished)
 002.8  De Ordi[..]   (paragraph start, flourished D extending into margin)
 002.9  et Ill(ustrissi)mi Do[..]   ("Ill" with superscript "mi")
 002.10 inc(?) solum[..]
 002.11 solui(?) co(n)scern[..] / co(n)fecer[..]?
 002.12 bagarina(?) [..]
 002.13 cambellar[..] / cancellar(?)
 002.14 [..]uin(?) (cut off at foot)
Small fragment (bottom left): faint mirror-image offset text along its top edge (illegible); then large display letters "[.]seph" followed by a flourished capital (start of next word, cut off by tile edge).

image-003 (native tile, upper part of the right-hand paper leaf of face 1, nearly full width; right leaf edge visible at right). Lines counted from top of image-003. Overlaps image-002 (line starts). Hand: fast humanist cursive/chancery italic, light brown-grey ink, many suspensions with superscript letters; "q" with stroke; long ascender loops make readings uncertain. Many words below are tentative.
 003.0  (heading, centred) M . D xxxx(?)[.] . Die Martis . 2(?) . Martij
          [numerals after D: three or four x-like strokes and a final minim; exact count uncertain]
 003.1  Cum Cor[.] (sup. "mis") Arbitri(?) Regius Curia(?) suscepisset loquendi cu(m) Mag(?) (sup. "cis/us") Agent[..]
 003.2  Regijs ut datia(?) imposita(?) tollerentur, et collecte alterius Principis Subdi[..]
 003.3  vlterius no(n) imponerentur, Si[..]q(ue)(?) [..]dus(?) ab eo D(omi)no i(n) quo non sunt [..]
 003.4  Illud in quo D(omi)n(u)s fundoru(m) habitat(?) in[..]ere(?) e[x]/et [..]bilia(?) p(ro)(?) [..]tari(?)
 003.5  Regni(?) ipsos(?) Agentis(?) Regios ut i(n) R(everendissi)mo (sup. "mo") Iudici(?) Comunicata(?) co(n)tra[..]
 003.6  vt [..]dus(?) [in] vno ad aliud d(omi)niu(m)(?) possint co(n)duci: sub ea(?) forma la[..]
 003.7  R[..]q(?) & ro[..] facta(?) relatio(?) fuit(?).   [line short; paragraph ends]
 003.8  De Ordinationibus(?) vero insolitis innovandis(?) et collectis no(n) imponen[dis]
 003.9  et Ill(ustrissi)mi (sup. "mi") Do(mi)nij(?) Veneti(?) co(n)tentatum(?) vt palam mouere(?) Germanicam(?)/Gromanicam(?) quod
 003.10 nunc(?) solum(?) Verone solvant(?) in his lo(cis)(?) in quibus annis superiori[bus]
 003.11 solui co(n)sueuerant(?), nec mercatores q(ui) i(n) Germania [&](?) Alesp[..](?) -ex(?) va[..]
 003.12 bagarina(?)/hagarina(?) merces ducebant(?) Verona(m) [..]; et ipsas merces ibi [..]sto(?) vltro(?)
 003.13 cambellar(?)/co(m)pellat(?) [..]q(ue) eas o(mn)es q(ui)s(?) merces(?) quas superioribus annis p(ro)[..]
 003.14 [..] Ven(eti)(?) [..]e educebat(?) nu(n)c(?) et vendere(?) in prohibitione(?) co(n)tinere(?)   [lower half of letters cut by tile edge]
 Notes: dark vertical stain/crease runs through the 2nd-3rd words of lines 4-14. Paragraph break at 003.8 marked by outdented flourished "De".

image-005 (native tile, lower part of right-hand paper leaf, face 1). Lines counted from top of image-005. Lines 005.1-005.3 overlap 003.11-003.13 (not new text). Text ends at 005.11; blank lower third. Pencil slip lower right: "Stams, STA, Frag. 82-2r". Small hole at foot.
 005.1  = 003.11 (solui co(n)sueuerant ... Germania ... va[..])
 005.2  = 003.12 (bagarina(?) merces ducebant(?) Verona(m) ... ipsas merces ibi [..] vltro(?))
 005.3  = 003.13 (cambellar(?) [..]q(ue) eas o(mn)es ... superioribus annis p(ro)[..])
 005.4  do. Ven(eti)(?) [..]re educebat nu(n)c et remota(?) i(?)/o(mni)(?) prohibitio(n)e co(n)ducere(?)
 005.5  possint, Se(?) etia(m)(?) apud Ser(enissi)(sup. "um")m Reg(em)(?) [..]n(?) datios(?) et vectigalia
 005.6  insolita i(?) que sunt in ditione regia ad pristinum reducantur(?)/redigantur(?)
 005.7  et Collecte in futuru(m) Venetis Subditis no(n) imponant(ur)(?) p(ro) his
 005.8  bonis que sub ipso Rege possident, no(n) [..]d(?) de Subditis Regijs
 005.9  ex aduerso fiat, quod si Ill(ustrissi)(sup. "um")m Do(minium)(?) hoc facere noluerit(?)/voluerit(?), se/eo
 005.10 quoq(ue) no(n) videre [..] quo mo(do) ceteris duabus petitionibus satis-
 005.11 facere possi[t](?)
 Script notes: "q(ue)" with ꝗ-like loop; superscript suspensions ("mi","um","mo","mis","us") over abbreviated honorifics; colons and commas/virgules used as punctuation.

image-004 (native tile, lower-left of face 1). Right edge shows line starts of the paper leaf already read on 003/005 (solui / bagarina / cambellar / do. Ven / possint / insolita / et Collecte / bonis que / ex aduerso / quoq(ue) / facere) - overlap only, no new text.
Small fragment "Stams, STA, Frag. 82-1r" (pencil slip at foot), read here:
 004.1  [Io?]seph  [first letter(s) torn away; large fraktur-like display hand with hairline flourishes] then a large flourished capital (F? / R? / T?) and a following letter cut by the torn right edge
 004.2  Organista  [smaller formal hand, brown ink]
 004.3  Anno [..]  (written "Ao" with superscript, flourished A; rest torn away)
 Faint mirror-image offset of several lines of text along the top edge (illegible). A brownish round stain mid-leaf. Grey rectangle covers lower-left area in the image (not part of the object reading). Looks like a label / ownership or title inscription for an organist, not a text page.

image-006 (overview, face 2 = versos of the same two pieces).
 - Left: small fragment verso (slip "Stams, StA, Frag. 82-1v"); only mirror-image show-through of "[..]seph", "Organista", "Anno" from the recto plus a stain; no independent writing seen at this scale.
 - Right: paper leaf verso (slip "Stams, StA, Frag. 82-2v"), single column ~23 lines, same cursive hand, heavier staining, brown damp/foxing along right edge and foot. Several words struck through (lines ~2, ~10-11). Interlinear additions (e.g. above line 2 and line 13, "forsan"? above a late line). A paragraph break about 2/3 down begins with a flourished capital. Text runs to the foot; last line(s) damaged by stain and a hole.

image-007 (native tile, left half of face 2). Small fragment verso ("Stams, STA, Frag. 82-1v"): only reversed show-through of recto display script ("[..]seph" + capital, "Organista", "Anno") and a stain; no verso writing of its own. Right edge shows only the first letter or two of the paper-leaf verso lines (read on image-008).

image-008 (native tile, right half of face 2 = paper-leaf verso, "82-2v"). Read via three horizontal crops made at native resolution:
